system_prompt: You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.
a1_answer:
DESIGN/INDICATOR: Nickel phase volume fraction control in the anode support structure
THRESHOLD: Maintain nickel volume fraction between 30-35% throughout 200 redox cycles
RATIONALE: USER CONSTRAINT requires 200 start-stop cycles; this range prevents excessive expansion while maintaining percolation pathways for fuel

DESIGN/INDICATOR: Nickel particle size distribution control in the anode
THRESHOLD: Keep average nickel particle size below 200 nm with a narrow distribution (D90/D10 < 2.5) after 200 redox cycles
RATIONALE: USER CONSTRAINT requires maintaining power density; smaller particles reduce agglomeration and coarsening during redox cycling

DESIGN/INDICATOR: Anode-electrolyte interface stress management
THRESHOLD: Keep interfacial tensile stress below 150 MPa during thermal cycling from room temperature to 750°C
RATIONALE: USER CONSTRAINT requires maintaining sealing integrity; this threshold prevents crack initiation at the interface

DESIGN/INDICATOR: Redox cycling rate control
THRESHOLD: Limit oxygen partial pressure change rate to <0.1 atm/min during start/stop events
RATIONALE: USER CONSTRAINT requires 200 start-stop cycles; slower redox kinetics reduce mechanical shock to the microstructure

FALSIFICATION TEST: Accelerated redox cycling test with 500 cycles between reducing (5% H2 in N2) and oxidizing (air) atmospheres at 750°C, with power density measurement at 0.7 V after every 50 cycles. Failure is defined as power density dropping below 0.35 W/cm2, visible cracks at the anode-electrolyte interface via SEM, or delamination observed by acoustic emission monitoring during thermal cycling. The test must be completed within 3 months to validate the 5-year service life requirement.
